title: Public Health Indicators to be Published to Enable Public to Track Health Outcomes and System Pressures
what_it_is: Public Health Indicators to be Published to Enable Public to Track Health Outcomes and System Pressures

sections.label: Health data reporting frequency
sections.summary: The annual National Population Health Survey and MOH Budget Book publish lifestyle factors and key performance indicators, and health outcomes take time to evolve.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The annual National Population Health Survey covers lifestyle risk factors and practices such as smoking, screening and vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The annual MOH Revenue and Expenditure Estimates – that is, the Budget Book – also published various key performance indicators, such as life expectancy, mortality rates from diseases, disease prevalence, medical resources and so on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Health outcomes take time to shape and evolve, and it would not be appropriate to report fortnightly or monthly.

sections.label: Reviewing meaningful health measures
sections.summary: Tracking and measuring have costs, so measures must be meaningful and lead to better behaviours, and a review is ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: There is also cost to tracking and the measuring, so we want to make sure that whatever we decide on to measure must be meaningful, must then lead to better behaviours and the correct approaches to then respond to some of those indicators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But I do take the point and we are actually reviewing to see what is a meaningful way to put out this information so that the public can understand, so that we can all track properly whether the good health outcomes are a result of the efforts that we are making.

sections.label: Reviewing health system measures
sections.summary: The matter will continue to be considered, with constant review of whether measures reflect the health system's state and prompt responses to ground needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As I said earlier, this is something that we will continue to consider.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But we do also have to appreciate that the information that we get is live, in terms of waiting times and all that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, the Member is right in that we will constantly review as to whether that measure is actually a good reflection of the state of the health systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But as you know, we give feedback all the time to MOH and we do respond quite immediately to some of these issues, especially with, say, waiting time at the polyclinics, how they are utilising the online systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: And on the go, our public healthcare providers are constantly trying to improve and adapt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, I want to give that assurance that we do take note of these: one, in respect of making sure that whatever we are measuring is meaningful; two, there is always a quick response to immediately and promptly respond to the needs on the ground as to the healthcare utilisation and to respond to the changing landscape with regard to ageing.
